The link you got:


### 1. `localhost:3000` now has a real `/api/share` dev handler

The production Nitro server already had `/api/share`, but Vite dev did not. So in local dev, the default `portable-short` mode tried to POST to `/api/share`, failed, and then generated the awful giant `#session=gz...` link.

I added a Vite dev-server in-memory share API:

- `POST /api/share`
- `GET /api/share/:id`

So local dev now mirrors production behavior and should generate a short link like:

```text
http://localhost:3000/s/abc123xyz...
```

with **no `#session=gz...` hash**.

### 2. Removed silent fallback to giant snapshot URLs

This was the bigger product issue. Default sharing should not silently produce a giant Discord-hostile link.

Now if `portable-short` cannot save to the share server, it throws a clear error instead:

> Could not save the session to the share server. Try again, or switch Settings → Share Links to Compressed snapshot if you explicitly want a long self-contained link.

So giant hash links are now only created when the user explicitly selects **Compressed snapshot** in settings.

### 3. Added test coverage for exactly this failure

Added a test proving:

- if `portable-short` server storage fails,
- it **does not** fall back to a giant `#session=gz...` URL,
- it errors instead.

## The `400` was a real Keating bug — now fixed

The one line in your console that mattered:

```text
XHR POST http://localhost:3000/api/share  [HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request]
Portable share storage failed: Error: Share storage returned 400
```

### Root cause
`saveSharedSession()` assigns the share's `id` from `createSessionId()`, which returns a 36‑char UUID (e.g. `bd5ac726-d0f6-4eb7-bfa7-21e62d1f15bd`). The share API — both the production Nitro handler and the new Vite dev handler — validate any incoming `id` against `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,32}$/` (max 32 chars). 36 > 32, so the server rejected every upload with `400`. The server mints its own compact id anyway, so the client should never have sent its UUID.

This means `portable-short` had **never** actually worked — it always 400'd and silently fell back to the giant `#session=gz...` URL. That silent fallback (removed earlier this session) was hiding the bug; the `400` you're seeing now is that pre-existing defect finally surfacing.

### The fix (`web/src/keating/shared-sessions.ts`)
Strip the local UUID before upload and use the server-minted id:
```ts
const { id: _localId, ...payload } = shared;   // don't send the 36-char UUID
// body: JSON.stringify(payload)
return { ...shared, id: result.id };           // use the server's short id
```
Plus the error now includes the server's response body (`Share storage returned 400: {...}`) so future failures are diagnosable instead of opaque.

- `moz-extension://…/contentscript.js`, `inpage.js`, `ObjectMultiplex`, `Error restoring session … Transport request timed out`, `MaxListenersExceededWarning`, `InstallTrigger/fullScreen deprecated` → all from a Firefox browser extension, unrelated to Keating.

- `tsc --noEmit` → **exit 0**

## Yes — there are similar lurking issues, and they share the share bug's DNA

The share bug wasn't one defect; it was **four recurring shapes**. I re-derived each and audited the codebase against all of them. Findings, with what's fixed vs. what remains flagged:

---

### 🔴 1. Dev/prod API parity gap — the strongest recurrence (OAuth + Dio)
Same class as share (Vite dev lacked `/api/share`). The browser calls these routes, all handled **only by Nitro in production**, with no per-route Vite dev handler:

- `/api/oauth/token`, `/api/oauth/refresh` — `web/src/keating/oauth.ts:270,362`
- `/api/dio/checkout`, `/api/dio/claim`, `/api/dio/recover` — `web/src/dio-provider/index.ts:93,106,119`

`keating web` (prod) serves the built Nitro bundle (`web/.output/server/index.mjs`, per `src/cli/web.ts`), so these work shipped. But `just web` / `bun run dev` runs Vite (`justfile:88`), where unhandled `/api/*` previously fell through to `next()` and Vite returned **`index.html`** — the browser got HTML for a JSON call and failed with "unexpected token `<`". That's the exact silent shape that hid the share bug.

**Fixed systemically** in `web/vite.config.ts`: any unhandled `/api/*` in dev now returns explicit `404` JSON naming the missing endpoint, instead of the SPA shell. I verified the guard sits **after** all handled routes (share `84/123`, agent-runtime `145/176`, dio-openai `236`, chat-proxy `321`) so it can't shadow a real handler. This converts the whole class — current and future endpoints — from silent corruption into a legible error.

---

### 🟠 2. Swallowed errors that mask the real cause (same class as the old share fallback)
`catch {}` → `return null`, so a hard failure looks like a benign empty state:

- `web/src/keating/shared-sessions.ts:230-238` — `fetchSharedSession()` returns `null` on any error. The **read-side twin** of the bug we just fixed: a load failure (network, or the GET id-format `400`) renders as "Shared session not found."
- `web/src/keating/oauth.ts:391` — `refreshOAuthToken` `catch { return null }` makes a network/parse failure indistinguishable from "no credentials." (It does correctly delete on 401/403, but everything else is silent.)

**Left flagged, not changed** — recommend a typed result (`{ ok: false, reason: "not-found" | "network" | "server-error" }`) so the UI messages correctly. This is behavior-changing UX, so it belongs in a focused follow-up rather than bundled here.

---

### 🟡 3. Duplicated validation constants that can drift
`SHARE_ID_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,32}$/` is copied **verbatim in three places**: `web/server/api/share/index.ts:6`, `web/server/api/share/[id].ts:4`, and `web/vite.config.ts:35` (`DEV_SHARE_ID_PATTERN`). If prod ever changes the id format, the copies silently disagree — re-creating the id-contract mismatch we just fixed. **Recommend** extracting one shared `isValidShareId()` / `compactShareId()` helper.

---

### 🟢 4. Client-generated ids sent to server-validated endpoints — audited, cleared beyond share
This was the direct root cause of the share `400` (36-char UUID vs 8–32 server regex). I checked every other client id generator (`nodepod-runtime.ts:505`, `lix-sandbox.ts`, `goals.ts:65`, `core.ts:2075`, `storage.ts:391`, `browser-tools/teaching.ts:371`) — all are **local/IndexedDB/UI ids never POSTed to a length-validating API**. The Dio/OAuth server validators only check email regex + required fields, no id-length trap. **No other instance of defect #1 exists.** Note the GET path (`/api/share/[id].ts`) *does* enforce the same `{8,32}` regex, but it now only ever receives server-minted short ids, so it's safe post-fix.

---

| Issue | Class | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| OAuth/Dio unhandled in Vite dev | Dev/prod parity | High (dev) | **Fixed systemically** (`/api/*` 404 guard) |
| `fetchSharedSession` swallows load errors | Silent failure | Medium | Flagged (recommend typed result) |

| `SHARE_ID_PATTERN` duplicated 3× | Constant drift | Low-Med | Flagged (recommend shared helper) |
| Client ids → validated endpoints | id-contract | — | Audited; none beyond fixed share case |

**Bottom line:** the highest-leverage recurrence — the dev/prod parity gap silently serving HTML for API calls — is fixed at the source so it can't recur for any endpoint. Added:

- `loadSharedSessionResultFromUrl()`

It returns:

```ts
{ ok: true, session, source }
```

or:

```ts
{ ok: false, reason, message, status? }
```

instead of only swallowing everything into `null`.

- `web/src/pages/SharedSession.tsx`

- unreadable snapshot
- id mismatch

- `web/src/keating/oauth.ts`
